ruling_text:
Mercedes-Benz Vehicle Trust, a Delaware statutory trust, successor by merger to Daimler Trust vs. Williams

Motion to Set Aside/Vacate Default
Defendant Cylinder Enterprises, Inc. dba Finish Line Towing and
Transport's Motion for Relief from Default is GRANTED. (Code
Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b).)
"[W]ith respect to setting aside a default judgment, it is the policy
of the law to favor, whenever possible, a hearing on the merits."
(Luxury Asset Lending, LLC v. Philadelphia Television Network,
Inc. (2020) 56 Cal.App.5th 894, 907.)
"The law favors judgments based on the merits, not procedural
missteps. Our Supreme Court has repeatedly reminded us that in
this area doubts must be resolved in favor of relief." (Lasalle v.
Vogel (2019) 36 Cal.App.5th 127, 134.)
Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) provides: "the court shall,
whenever an application for relief is made no more than six
months after entry of judgment, is in proper form, and is
accompanied by an attorney's sworn affidavit attesting to the
attorney's mistake, inadvertence, surprise, or neglect, vacate any
(1) resulting default entered by the clerk against the
attorney's client, and which will result in entry of a default
judgment, or (2) resulting default judgment or dismissal entered
against the attorney's client, unless the court finds that the default
or dismissal was not in fact caused by the attorney's mistake,
inadvertence, surprise, or neglect..."
Moving Defendant's default was entered on 7/31/25 and this
motion was filed on 10/5/25, which is within the six month time
limit to bring this motion.
Moving Defendant has submitted the proposed responsive
pleadings as exhibits 17 and 18 to the Declaration of Ramshin
Daneshi, Esq. (ROA 63.)
Moving Defendant has submitted the declaration of Martin R. Fox,
Esq. to establish that the default was taken as a result of Mr. Fox's
mistake, inadvertence, surprise or neglect. (See ROA 59 - Fox
Decl. at ¶¶19-22; 25; and 31.)
Plaintiff opposes the motion, arguing that mandatory relief under
Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) is not available because the default
was not “solely caused by Defendant’s attorney.” (Opp. at 9:1-9:4.)
Plaintiff reasons that because Defendant was served with a
summons that their failure to file a responsive pleading cannot be
the result of Defendant’s attorney’s mistake, inadvertence, surprise
or neglect. Plaintiff also argues that where the attorney’s mistake
in permitting the entry of default is “the result of professional
incompetence, general ignorance of the laws, or unjustifiable
negligence in discovering the law” then mandatory relief under
Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) is not warranted. (See Opp. at
10:4-10:8 [citing Henderson v. Pacific Gas & Electric Co. (2010)
187 Cal.App.4th 215, 229].) Plaintiff’s reliance on Henderson is
misplaced. Henderson found that the mandatory relief provision of
Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) was not available to relieve a party
of a dismissal entered after a motion for summary judgment was
granted, and the language cited from Henderson in Plaintiff’s
Opposition deals with the assessment of a request for discretionary
relief. Since Mr. Fox’s declaration satisfies the court that the
default was entered solely as a result of neglect on the part of
Moving Defendant’s attorney, the requirements for mandatory
relief under Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) have been met and the
default shall be set aside on that basis.
Code Civ. Proc. §473, subd. (b) further provides “[t]he court shall,
whenever relief is granted based on an attorney’s affidavit of fault,
direct the attorney to pay reasonable compensatory legal fees and
costs to opposing counsel or parties.” Accordingly, within 30 days,
Moving Defendant’s attorney of record, MFox Law Group, Inc.
shall pay $999 to Plaintiff to compensate Plaintiff for the
reasonable legal fees and costs incurred as a result of Moving
Defendant’s failure to timely respond to the Complaint.
Moving Defendant shall separately file and serve the proposed
responsive pleadings attached as Exhibits 17 [Answer] and 18
[Cross-Complaint] to the Declaration of Ramshin Daneshi, Esq.
within 5 days of this ruling. Separate e-filing is necessary to ensure
the pleadings are properly indexed by the Court’s electronic filing
system.
Moving Defendants shall provide notice of this ruling.
Parties/counsel are ordered to call Department C44 to advise if
parties/counsel submit on the tentative or wish to be heard. If the
parties wish to argue, the motion will be continued to March 26,
2026 at 8:30 a.m. for oral argument.
